sections.html:
With a cash buyer, nobody waits on a bank's sign-off, so closing can land on whatever date suits you, frequently inside a month. The price is lower than a polished listing might reach. Weigh the offer against a listing estimate before saying yes.

New Braunfels now counts 122,492 residents, up 35.5 percent since the 2020 base. Fast growth fills the market with newer builds, and an aging house has to stand out among them.

Common reasons owners here pick a fast sale:

  • A move up or down the I-35 corridor toward Austin or San Antonio.
  • Repair needs that scare off buyers using loans.
  • A vacation or short-term rental that stopped earning its keep.
  • Inherited property split between several heirs.
  • A code, title or tax snag.

sections.h2: Which county is your house in?
sections.html:
The city is the seat of Comal County, yet its limits spill into Guadalupe County too. A parcel can land in either one. Check the tax bill: whichever appraisal district sends it is the one that values your lot, and that county's clerk is the office that will file your deed.

Many buyers are coming from the San Antonio side or commuting along Interstate 35 and Farm Road 725. Streets near Landa Park and the rivers hold the German-era housing, while the outer edge is mostly recent subdivisions. Tell a buyer which type you own, and disclose any flooding or drainage trouble, because the rivers affect plenty of lots.

sections.h2: Home values and the local market
sections.html:
Prices here sit well above what smaller Texas towns see. Plenty of owners hold their homes for years, so a visibly worn house is easy for buyers to pass over.

Commuting buyers tend to prefer a house they can move into without a renovation. If yours needs work, an investor may be the better fit than a family.

sections.h2: Appraisal district and property tax rules
sections.html:
Comal County parcels go through the Comal Appraisal District, which sets values and processes exemptions from its office at 900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels. It keeps weekday hours, and April 15 and May 15 are the dates it highlights. A Guadalupe County parcel belongs to a different district, so ask that county's tax office who appraises it.

The school district exemption for homeowners is $140,000. Once a homestead exemption is in place, the appraised value cannot climb more than 10 percent a year, starting the January 1 after the exemption first applies. Senior and disabled owners can have school taxes frozen.

  • Value date: January 1.
  • Protest deadline: mid-May in most cases.
  • Delinquency: February 1, after a January 31 due date.

That cap protects long-time owners and resets when the house sells, so the next owner may see a bigger bill. Mention it when you discuss price.

sections.h2: Selling a rented or short-term rental house
sections.html:
With so many river and lake visitors, lots of homes here have hosted short stays. A tenant in place controls your timeline. Texas landlords serve a written notice to vacate, three days unless the lease says otherwise, and only then can ask a justice court to act.

Phone the City of New Braunfels about any permit or registration your short-term rental carries before the transfer, since the rules can vary by address. Investors will ask for the rental history and any open compliance issue.

Move quickly if payments have slipped. After a default notice you have 20 days to bring the loan current. Foreclosure auctions take place on the first Tuesday of the month at a spot the commissioners court designates, and the sale posting must go up at least three weeks beforehand.

Property taxes follow a separate clock. A lien attaches every January 1, penalties and interest start after February 1, and a taxing unit that hires a private attorney can add a collection penalty of up to 20 percent. Both payoffs are settled from your proceeds at closing. The title company can give you the exact figures.

sections.h2: Cash offer, listing or family sale
sections.html:
Condition and timing decide this. A cash offer works for a house needing repairs or an owner facing a hard deadline, while a polished house in a strong subdivision may net more on the open market.

  • Cash offer: no repairs, you choose the date, no financing contingency.
  • Traditional listing: higher potential price, plus commissions, repairs and showings.
  • Sale to an heir or relative: may need a deed and clear title paperwork.

Get written offers and compare what you would keep after payoffs and fees.

sections.h2: How a quick sale unfolds, step by step
sections.html:
Gather your latest tax bill, mortgage statement and any lease. Collect written offers from more than one buyer and set them next to a realistic listing estimate for the same house.

After you accept, the title company opens a file, searches for liens and unpaid taxes, and schedules signing. A clean title leaves little between you and your chosen closing date. A lien, a missing heir or a tenant changes that, so have the buyer put any new timeline in writing.

Never pay anyone upfront just to receive an offer. A fair buyer covers the closing costs spelled out in the contract, and every line should be visible before you sign.

Ask who actually pays for the title policy, whether the offer changes after an inspection, and how many days the buyer needs to close. Find out whether the buyer plans to fix and resell, rent the place out, or move in, because that plan decides how much repair risk they will take on and shows directly in the number.

Request proof of funds. A buyer paying cash should be able to show it. Ask for the earnest money amount too, and whether it comes back to you if the deal fails for a reason that is not your fault.

Keep the answers in writing. Two offers that look alike on the first page can differ a lot once fees, repair credits and the closing date are added in.

The title company drafts the deed and the settlement statement. The clerk of the county where the land sits records it, and your signature must be notarized or otherwise officially acknowledged first.

Recording starts at five dollars for the first page. Call the Comal County Clerk, or the Guadalupe County Clerk if that is where your parcel lies, for the current schedule.

On closing day bring photo ID, payoff details for any loan, and every key and garage opener. Payoffs and any tax owed are subtracted, then you receive the balance. Because a cash sale skips the lender appraisal and underwriting, those are two common stumbling blocks you avoid.

faqs.q: How fast can a New Braunfels sale close?
faqs.a: Often in a few weeks when title is clear. A shared inheritance, a lien or a tenant adds time. Put the closing date in writing with the offer.

faqs.q: Is New Braunfels in Comal or Guadalupe County?
faqs.a: Both. The city is the Comal County seat and stretches into Guadalupe County. The appraisal district named on your tax bill tells you which applies.

faqs.q: What does a typical New Braunfels house cost?
faqs.a: The median owner-held home value is $339,400. Condition, location and size move your own price, so use that number only as background.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Braunfels house with foundation or roof problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers absorb the repairs and price them into the offer. Hold it up against a repaired listing estimate to see which nets more.

faqs.q: When are New Braunfels property tax protests due?
faqs.a: Mid-May in most cases. April 15 and May 15 are the dates the Comal Appraisal District highlights, so call the office to confirm yours.
